Subject: Discovery recap: pricing & token economics — Aurora pilot

Thanks again for the time today, Alice — quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call. I kept this focused on the cost/pricing items procurement flagged.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Primary workload: multi-turn patient summarization + secure QA search (avg context length ~1.5k tokens).
- Expected pilot volume: 2–5M tokens/month for first 3 months; potential scale to 30–60M tokens/month in year 1 if adoption goes well.
- SLOs: p95 latency <800ms, prefer hosted but open to a dedicated pool if we need predictable throughput.
- Procurement asks: line-item invoice with unit economics ($/1M tokens), overage policy, and a sample invoice/estimate for budgeting.

Rough qualification numbers (do not share outside of Aurora procurement until we confirm):
- Target Aurora budget band: indicated ~$50k–$120k/month for production (we should confirm whether that is for gross platform spend or net after discounts).
- Target unit economics requested: between $60–$110 per 1M tokens (Aurora asked for a target $/1M to compare alternatives).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a short invoice-style estimate and a lightweight pricing calculator with three scenarios (pilot, scale, dedicated reserved).
2) We’ll include assumptions for caching, batching, and typical tokenization for your document mix.
3) If the numbers look good, we’ll produce a draft invoice (PDF) and a 30-day pilot SOW.

Can you confirm the 2–5M monthly pilot range and whether procurement needs the invoice routed to a specific AP contact?

Thanks,
Markus
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus — that summary is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we loop procurement: 

1) The 2–5M pilot number is correct for the initial trial. For budgeting we need a sample monthly invoice for both a conservative (2M) and baseline (5M) scenario.
2) Procurement wants the line items broken out: model compute, tokens (prompt vs completion), data retention/storage, and any integration/setup fees.
3) On unit economics, can you show the impact of caching (prefix cache) and batching? Our engineering lead says ~25% of tokens are repeated prefixes across calls.

Also — are there explicit overage rates if we exceed the committed volume during the pilot? We prefer clear per-unit overage rather than auto-scaling charges.

AP contact for invoice routing is: Cynthia Lo <cynthia.lo@aurora.health>. Procurement also asked for an estimate in XLSX format they can attach to the PO.

If you can send something by EOD Thu (PST) that would be ideal.

Hi Alice — attached are the XLSX estimator and a CSV copy of the calculator so procurement can ingest it. Attachment stubs below. I also pasted a short, line-item estimate for 2 scenarios to make review faster.

Attachment: aurora-pricing-estimate-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 28 KB)
Attachment: aurora-pricing-calculator.csv (csv, 6 KB)

Assumptions used (please review):
- Tokenization: avg 1,500 tokens per request (prompt+response); split 40% prompt / 60% completion.
- Caching: prefix dedupe assumed at 25% token reduction on prompt tokens (applies to 40% of total tokens).
- Batching/throughput: we assume continuous batching at 75% efficiency for the hosted tier; dedicated reserved would increase batching efficiency to ~90%.
- Model tiers: Gen-A (high quality) vs Gen-B (cost-optimized quantized). Prices below are per 1M input+output tokens.

Scenario A — Pilot (2M tokens/month)
- Gen-A (hosted): list price equivalent $180 / 1M tokens -> base estimate: $360/month
- Gen-B (quantized host): $45 / 1M tokens -> base estimate: $90/month
- With caching (25% effective on prompts) and batching, blended estimate (Gen-A pilot realistic): $128 / 1M tokens -> $256/month
- Line items (example): compute + infra $170, token processing $60, storage/retention $26

Scenario B — Baseline (5M tokens/month)
- Gen-A blended with caching & batching: $96 / 1M tokens -> $480/month
- Dedicated reserved pool (monthly commit, 12-month): blended $72 / 1M tokens for 5M+ commits -> $360/month

Overage policy (pilot): overage charged at published rate per 1M based on the model tier used in that month; we can cap overage at 20% above committed monthly volume if you prefer a soft cap.

Notes on unit economics and how to hit target $/1M:
- If Aurora can commit to a 12-month reserved pool at 30–50M tokens/month, we can hit $40–$60 / 1M for quantized variants.
- Caching and prompt engineering are the fastest levers to reduce per-token cost for your workload.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm which model tier you want us to base the invoice on (Gen-A vs Gen-B).
2) Confirm whether procurement wants a dedicated reserved quote or hosted line items.
3) I’ll produce a draft invoice PDF and a short SOW for the pilot that includes a 30-day early-termination clause.

If that all looks OK I’ll send the PDF invoice draft and ask Marissa to review discounts for first-year volume.

Thanks,
Markus
